spec_architectural_decisions.decision: export_logs keeps GRANT ALL (single invekto role) and is made append-only at the application layer (ExportRepository issues INSERT only; no UPDATE/DELETE statements target export_logs).
spec_architectural_decisions.reason: Project canon (codex-context.md L20/L69) is GRANT ALL; a prior package (B1) FAILED review for downgrading it. There is no separate audit-writer DB role in this architecture.
spec_architectural_decisions.codex_note: EXPECTED: do NOT flag GRANT ALL on export_logs as a least-privilege violation. Append-only is enforced in code, not via column grants, by design.

spec_architectural_decisions.decision: PDF bytes are generated in the browser (jsPDF); the server only serves report-data JSON and writes the export_logs row with delivery_mode='client_render'. status='completed' means 'export data served', not 'PDF physically rendered/downloaded'.
spec_architectural_decisions.reason: Literal server-side HTML->PDF would force Chromium/wkhtmltopdf onto the prod Outbound microservice (zero browser runtime today). PDF payload is small and bounded (summary + <=2000 rows).
spec_architectural_decisions.codex_note: EXPECTED: do NOT flag the browser-side PDF generation or the 'completed=data served' audit semantics as a silent-failure or audit gap; delivery_mode column + report-data forensic fields disclose this honestly.

spec_architectural_decisions.decision: Export feature is gated by tenant-scoped JWT + ExportOptions(Enabled,AllowAllTenants); there is NO per-operator export RBAC.
spec_architectural_decisions.reason: The codebase has no granular operator-permission model (tenant-scoped JWT only); Q's interview answer was 'all tenants/operators can export'.
spec_architectural_decisions.codex_note: EXPECTED: do NOT flag missing per-operator export permissions; tenant isolation is the authorization boundary by product decision.

spec_architectural_decisions.decision: custom_fields (JSONB) is exported as a single JSON-string column, not flattened into dynamic per-key columns.
spec_architectural_decisions.reason: Dynamic column expansion is unbounded (column-explosion DoS) and non-deterministic across rows.
spec_architectural_decisions.codex_note: EXPECTED: single custom_fields column is intentional, not a missed flattening.

plan.summary: FEAT-OBI Phase 1A Plan B: an Export Manager that lets an operator export their contact lists (list_records) and bulk-send campaign results (per-recipient delivery status + campaign summary) as CSV / Excel / PDF, with an export_logs KVKK audit trail. All data is in Postgres; no INMA dependency.
plan.q_intent: Plan A live -> start Plan B (Export Manager): export_logs table + export endpoints + ExportManagerPage. Interview answers: export lists+send results; server-side + export_logs; CSV+Excel+PDF; all tenants (Outbound plan); PDF = both summary report + capped table; PDF via HTML->PDF no-license. 'devam'.
plan.interview_notes: 6 interview Qs resolved. Key architecture tension surfaced + resolved with Q approval ('devam'): 'server-side generation' + 'HTML->PDF no-license' would force Chromium/wkhtmltopdf onto the prod Outbound microservice. PDF payload is small/bounded, so: CSV+XLSX generated server-side and streamed (Q's literal choice, export_logs audit); PDF (report + <=2000-row capped table) rendered in-browser (jsPDF+autotable) from a server report-data JSON endpoint that STILL writes an export_logs row on ?for=pdf -> identical audit across all 3 formats, no native browser runtime on prod. Send-results delivery status is fully captured in outbound_messages (status/sent_at/delivered_at/read_at/failed_reason), linked via bulk_send_jobs.broadcast_ids. PDF applies to send results only, not raw contact lists. Tenant gate reuses Plan A ContactListOptions (Enabled+AllowAllTenants), already enabled in prod.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Migration 053 creates export_logs (tenant_id FK, export_type/format CHECKs, GRANT ALL) idempotently with a DO $verify$ INV-SEED-053 postcondition; outbound.sql canonical mirror updated.

Operator can export a contact list as CSV (UTF-8 BOM + formula-injection escaping) and XLSX (ClosedXML) server-side; the file streams with correct Content-Disposition and an export_logs row is written (export_type=contact_list, correct format + row_count).

Bulk-send campaign export bases on the bulk_send_recipients snapshot LEFT JOIN outbound_messages (never-sent recipients appear with status=not_sent, never silently dropped), with a tenant_id predicate on every joined table and a defined status precedence (read>delivered>sent>sending>queued>failed>blocked>not_sent); per-recipient CSV/XLSX carries status + timestamps, plus a campaign summary; each writes an export_logs row.

PDF export (report page + <=2000-row capped recipient table) is rendered in the browser from GET report-data?for=pdf; the server writes an export_logs row (format=pdf) at data-serve time; over-cap requests are handled (cap note in PDF, INV-OB-058 only if a hard limit is exceeded).

Every export query is tenant-scoped and verifies source ownership (list/job belongs to the JWT tenant) -> INV-OB-055 otherwise; the whole feature is gated by the new ExportOptions (Enabled + AllowAllTenants) -> INV-OB-056 when disabled; no cross-tenant data leak.

Backend proxies the 3 export routes to Outbound with JWT->tenant auth, streaming file responses through without buffering and preserving Content-Type/Content-Disposition; full .NET solution build + SPA build PASS.

build.note: Full .NET solution build 0 errors; SPA build (tsc + vite) clean. ClosedXML 0.104.2 + jspdf/jspdf-autotable restored.

verification_questions.question: Does every export data query and export_logs insert scope strictly by tenant_id AND verify that the requested data_lists.id / bulk_send_jobs.id belongs to the JWT tenant, so a tenant cannot export another tenant's contacts or campaign delivery status by guessing an id?

Is the per-recipient send-results join correct and tenant-safe: does it read outbound_messages WHERE tenant_id = @tenant AND broadcast_id = ANY(bulk_send_jobs.broadcast_ids), rather than trusting client-supplied broadcast ids, and does it handle a job with empty broadcast_ids (no recipients) without error?

Are all DB paths in ExportRepository wrapped to catch BOTH NpgsqlException and PostgresException and mapped to INV-OB-057 (not a generic 500), and does an export failure write an export_logs row with status=failed + error_code (no silent failure)?

Does the Backend proxy stream large export file bodies through to the client without fully buffering them in memory, and preserve Content-Type + Content-Disposition, so a 50k-row XLSX/CSV download does not OOM the Backend or lose the filename?

Is formula-injection hardening (leading = + - @ and leading TAB/CR/LF escaped) applied to BOTH CSV and XLSX user-controlled fields, is CSV emitted UTF-8 with BOM so Turkish characters render in Excel, and are phone/id cells written as text in XLSX (no scientific notation / leading-zero loss / no AdjustToContents at 50k)?

Does the campaign per-recipient export base on bulk_send_recipients LEFT JOIN outbound_messages (so a recipient with no message row is exported as not_sent rather than dropped by an inner join), apply a deterministic status-precedence when more than one message matches, and never trust broadcast_ids without a tenant_id predicate on outbound_messages?

forbidden_areas: src/Invekto.Outbound/Services/MessageSenderService.cs (INMA bridge - export is read-only, never sends)
bulk_send_recipients / bulk_send_jobs schema (read-only consumers, no DDL changes)
data_lists / list_records schema (Plan A, read-only here)
non_goals: INMA MSSQL contact pull/export (Faz 1 INMA-approval blocker - out of scope)
Phone masking (operators need raw phones for reuse; export_logs is the KVKK control)
Server-side PDF generation via Chromium/wkhtmltopdf (deliberately rejected to keep prod Outbound free of a browser runtime)
A new feature flag (reuse Plan A ContactListOptions)
intentional_exclusions: PDF for raw contact lists (impractical at 50k rows; CSV/XLSX only) - PDF is send-results only
True streaming XLSX (ClosedXML builds in-memory; acceptable at the 50k cap)
Reconciling export_logs status=completed against actual browser PDF render success (log = data-served; documented)

user_facing_errors: INV-OB-055 ExportSourceNotFound (list/campaign not found or not owned by tenant)
error_handling.silent_failure_explanation: Every export path writes an export_logs row (completed or failed+error_code). DB exceptions are typed-caught (Npgsql+Postgres) -> INV-OB-057, never swallowed. A failed PDF data-serve returns a mapped error; the only accepted gap (documented) is that export_logs=completed means 'data served', not 'browser PDF rendered', which is a benign over-count for an audit trail.

aha_moments.user_pain: Clinic owner wants to show their boss/partner a clean campaign result they can forward, not a raw spreadsheet of phone numbers.
aha_moments.suggestion: The PDF campaign report leads with a shareable summary card (sent / delivered / read / failed + opt-out skips + template + dates) before the recipient table.
aha_moments.aha_moment: Operator clicks 'PDF' and gets a client-ready one-pager they can email to the clinic owner in seconds.

aha_moments.user_pain: After a bulk send, the operator has no idea which numbers actually got the message vs failed/blocked.
aha_moments.suggestion: The per-recipient export includes a human-readable status column (Teslim edildi / Okundu / Basarisiz / Engellendi-optout) plus the timestamps, not just an internal code.
aha_moments.aha_moment: Operator opens the CSV and instantly sees exactly who to follow up with by phone.

aha_moments.user_pain: KVKK exposure: nobody can prove who exported customer phone lists or when, if there's ever a complaint.
aha_moments.suggestion: export_logs records tenant, operator identity, list/campaign, row count, format, and timestamp for every single export.
aha_moments.aha_moment: When asked 'who exported our patient list?', the answer is one query away with a full audit trail.

aha_moments.user_pain: Re-uploading the same contacts every time is tedious; operators want round-trip between import and export.
aha_moments.suggestion: Contact-list export emits a CSV whose columns match the Plan A import mapper exactly, so an exported list re-imports cleanly (edit-in-Excel round-trip).
aha_moments.aha_moment: Operator exports a list, fixes a few rows in Excel, re-imports it with zero column re-mapping.

aha_moments.user_pain: Support can't help a confused operator because they can't see what the operator's export actually contained.
aha_moments.suggestion: export_logs row_count + status let support confirm 'your export had 1,240 rows and completed at 14:32' without touching the operator's machine.
aha_moments.aha_moment: Support resolves an 'export is missing rows' ticket from the audit log instead of a screen-share.

aha_moments.user_pain: A 50k-row list dumped to PDF would be a useless 800-page document.
aha_moments.suggestion: PDF caps the recipient table at 2,000 rows with a visible 'showing first 2,000 of N - use CSV/Excel for full data' note, while CSV/XLSX carry the full set.
aha_moments.aha_moment: Operator never gets a broken/huge PDF and is steered to the right format automatically.
